title: Seamark trace v3
description: What an agent did, in one shape whatever observed it. The capture level on every event is what decides what the document may claim: a trace read from the agent's own transcript cannot assert authenticity, and says so rather than leaving the field out. Field names follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions where those have one. Arguments and results travel as sha256 digests, because these files hold somebody's conversation; the literal content appears only when the caller asked for it. Nothing here is a summary and nothing here is a number standing in for evidence. What v2 changes over v1, and why none of it fitted inside v1: MCP revision 2026-07-28 removed protocol-level sessions and the initialize handshake (SEP-2567, SEP-2575), so the facts that used to be established once per session - the protocol revision, the client, the server, and the key by which two messages belong to one run - are now carried by every message and are recorded per event here. Seven gap reasons are added with them, and widening a closed enum narrows nothing for a producer and everything for a consumer that switches exhaustively, which is the rule that makes this a new version rather than an addition to the old one. trace/v1 stays published and stays readable. What v3 changes over v2: six fields that carried a value chosen by a third party now carry a salted REFERENCE to it instead - session_id, gen_ai.conversation.id, gen_ai.tool.call.id, the gap's after_event, mcp.client, mcp.server and mcp.request.state. Correlation is unchanged, because one value gives one reference within a session; what is gone is the value. That is a change to what those fields MEAN, which this project's compatibility rule makes a new version rather than an amendment, including when the version being amended is twenty minutes old and has no consumer - 'nobody was using that one' is the argument schemas/__init__.py refuses by name. trace/v1 and trace/v2 stay published and stay readable. Which fields are referenced, which travel literally and why, and which the reader refuses outright, are all in src/seamark/trace/provenance.py, and a test fails if this contract grows a field that table does not classify.

session_id.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. The session this trace is about, as the source named it.

source.description: What produced the trace: an agent's own transcript reader, or a proxy.

versions.description: Every version of the agent that wrote part of the bytes this trace was derived from. A list rather than one string because the format is the agent's internal one and it changes between releases.

state.description: not_evaluated means the question does not apply at this capture level, which is the L0 case: the audited agent wrote the transcript itself. not_established means it applied and could not be answered, which is a failure. The two are kept apart because conflating them is how a tool ends up claiming what it never observed.

applies.description: Whether the capture level is one at which authenticity is a question at all.

complete.description: True only when something recorded that the session ended AND nothing recorded a hole. Failure is the default: an absence of bad news is not good news. A capture level whose format has no end-of-session record therefore never produces a complete trace, and says so in an `end_not_recorded` hole rather than assuming the file was finished.

child_returncode.description: The exit code of the watched command, when there was one. Deliberately not part of completeness: a trace of a failed run is a complete trace of a failed run.

gaps.description: Everything that happened and was not observed, with where in the order it sits and why.

blind_spots.description: What this capture level cannot see at all, declared by the level rather than inferred per session. A question outside the level is unanswerable, never answered False.

duplicate_records_collapsed.description: How many records the source wrote for a call it had already recorded, collapsed onto the one event that call is. A fact about the source that this document does not otherwise carry, because the collapsed records are not in it. Absent means nobody counted, which is not zero.

mcp.description: What the protocol said about itself during this run. Absent means nobody looked, which is not the same as nothing having been declared.

protocol_revisions_observed.description: Every distinct MCP revision observed across this run's events, sorted. More than one is a fact about the run, not an error.

ref.description: The salted reference to the server, resolvable only against the operator's own `interposition.json`.

tools_advertised.description: What `server/discover` (SEP-2575) said this server offered at the moment of the run. A server with no entry here produced no observed discover result and carries a `discover_unavailable` hole instead of an empty list.

capture_level.description: L0 the agent's own transcript; L1 an MCP proxy; L2 a network proxy; L3 a seccomp sandbox. L2 and L3 are named so a rule can refuse by name before they exist.

index.description: Position in this document, consecutive from zero. What a non-conformance cites.

gen_ai.tool.call.id.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. The id the source issued for this call. A gap anchors to it (D-258), and it anchors just as well referenced as it did literally.

gen_ai.conversation.id.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. The conversation this call belongs to.

result_sha256.description: Null means the result was never recorded, which is a gap, and not that the result was empty.

error.type.description: Set when the tool itself reported a failure. An observed failure is not a missing observation.

sidechain.description: Whether the call came from a sub-agent of the same session.

gen_ai.tool.call.arguments.description: The literal arguments. Present only when the caller explicitly asked to keep content.

gen_ai.tool.call.result.description: The literal result. Present only when the caller explicitly asked to keep content.

traceparent.description: The W3C trace context this message carried in `_meta` (SEP-414). It is what replaced the session id SEP-2567 removed, and it is the only key by which two observed messages can be said to belong to one run. Null means the message carried none, which is a `no_correlation_key` hole and never a key of this tool's own invention.

mcp.protocol.version.description: The MCP revision this event's message declared in `_meta`. Per event rather than per session because the handshake that stated it once is gone, and two messages of one run may legitimately declare different revisions. Null is `protocol_version_unknown`: a proxy that does not know which revision it is interposing does not know what it is looking at.

mcp.client.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. The client software that sent the call, from `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`.

mcp.server.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. The server software that answered, from `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`, which SEP-2575 asks servers to put in every result.

mcp.result.type.description: SEP-2322's required `resultType`. `input_required` is the interim result of a multi round-trip request, which is one logical call seen twice.

mcp.result.type_assumed.description: True when the server omitted `resultType` and this reader supplied `complete`, which the specification requires of a reader. It travels because an assumption published as the server's own statement is exactly what this document refuses to do anywhere else.

mcp.request.state.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. SEP-2322's `requestState` on an `input_required` result: the only thing that pairs that result with the retry that follows it. The specification has servers encode their own identifier in it, which is why it is referenced rather than matched against a set of permitted characters. Null is `input_state_absent`, and the pairing is then not made - never by arrival order.

after_index.description: Where `after_event` sits in this document's events. Present only when the identity resolves to exactly one event here; otherwise `after_index_absent` is present instead. Never -1: a hole before every event has no index, it has a reason.

reason.description: A closed vocabulary. An open one is how `unknown` becomes the commonest value.

after_event.description: A salted reference to the value, not the value: `H(session salt || value)`, truncated. Two events carrying one value carry one reference, so every correlation a reader could make from the value itself still holds; the value is resolvable only from the operator's own map, beside their records and never in this document. See src/seamark/trace/provenance.py. The `gen_ai.tool.call.id` of the event this hole sits after. Absent when the hole is not attributable to a position between two observed events.

after_index_absent.description: Why this hole cites no position. Present exactly when `after_index` is not, so a consumer can never read a missing anchor as position zero.

gap.description: A hole, anchored to the IDENTITY of the event it follows rather than to a position. The position is resolved against this document's events when the document is written, so it cannot go stale when the events are ordered; when there is no event to anchor to, `after_index` is ABSENT and `after_index_absent` says why. An invented position is indistinguishable from a measured one.
